data.why: A park pond in section with a big storybook fish in it, built cut open like an anatomy plate so its organs face the camera, and a leaf floating on the water. The story follows the water into the fish (mouth, rakers, gills, covers) and then the fish up to the surface: it sinks, gets a swim bladder, drifts, gets a tail, swings, gets fins, needs oxygen, gets gills, clogs, gets rakers, stops, gets covers, warm water runs low, it rises, a heron spots it, a dark back, a strike, a lateral line, a scrape, scales. The camera stays close on the fish and pulls out to the pond at the end.

ideas.idea: a tube of meat in a pond is the start of a fish
meat is denser than water and goes to the bottom
a gas-filled swim bladder makes it float
floating is not moving: it just hangs there
a tail pushes it forward
each push of the tail turns the whole body
fins keep it straight
swimming uses oxygen, and it has no way to get any
water goes in at the mouth and over red gills that take its oxygen
the water brings grit that clogs the gills
gill rakers comb the grit out first
a fish at rest moves no water over its gills
gill covers pump water through even at rest
warm water holds little oxygen
it goes up to the surface where the water is richer
at the surface a heron sees the bright fish
a dark back hides it against the mud
the heron still aims at the dark shape
a lateral line feels the beak's ripple so it gets away
this is the lateral line
the warning comes late and the beak scrapes its skin
scales and slime protect the skin
lily pads on the pond and the fish swims across
you have built a fish

surprises.claim: A swim bladder is a gas-filled organ that lets a bony fish control how it floats
surprises.search: swim bladder gas filled organ buoyancy bony fish

surprises.claim: Gill rakers are comb-like projections on the gill arches that keep particles away from the gill filaments
surprises.search: gill rakers function filter particles protect gill filaments

surprises.claim: Fresh water holds about 14.6 milligrams of oxygen per liter at 0 degrees Celsius but only about 7.6 at 30 degrees

sentences.text: If you drop a tube of meat in a pond, you have a fish.
But meat is heavier than water, so it sinks.
So you give it a swim bladder full of gas.
But the bladder only floats it, so it drifts.
So you add a tail that sweeps it forward.
But every tail sweep swings its whole body sideways.
So you add fins that hold it straight.
But the fins keep it swimming, which burns oxygen.
So it gulps water through its mouth and over red gills.
But the water it gulps carries grit that clogs the gills.
So you add gill rakers, a comb that catches grit.
But when it stops, no water flows over the gills.
So you add gill covers that pump water at rest.
But on hot days, the water it pumps holds little oxygen.
So it rises to gulp the richer water at the surface.
But at the surface, a heron spots the bright fish.
So you give it a dark back like the mud.
But the heron still strikes at the dark back.
So you add a lateral line that feels the ripple.
This is the lateral line.
But the line is late, and the beak scrapes its skin.
So you cover it in scales and slime.
Add lily pads, and let it swim across the pond.
Congratulations, you have built a fish.
